message.content:
Below is a **gcloud** command that will create a Compute Engine instance on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
Feel free to adjust the values (e.g., `--zone`, `--machine-type`, `--project`) to match your environment.

```bash
# Create a Compute Engine instance with an RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS
gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-a6000-instance \
    --zone=us-central1-a \                     # <-- change to your preferred zone
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \             # <-- 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \           # Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image family
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \          # Ubuntu official image project
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \                   # <-- size of the boot disk
    --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \             # <-- persistent disk type
    --boot-disk-device-name=my-rtx-a6000-disk \ # <-- name of the boot disk
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \   # <-- RTX A6000 GPU
    --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE \           # <-- instance will be terminated on host maintenance
    --restart-on-failure \                     # <-- automatically restart if it fails
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \ # <-- optional: custom startup script
    --tags=http-server,https-server \          # <-- optional: allow HTTP/HTTPS traffic
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \ # <-- full access scope
    --service-account=my-service-account@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com \ # <-- optional: custom service account
    --no-creation-error-check \                # <-- skip creation error check (optional)
    --quiet                                      # <-- suppress prompts
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | The Compute Engine zone where the instance will be created. |
| `--machine-type` | CPU & memory configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs and 30 GB RAM. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Specify the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | Size and type of the boot disk. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the RTX A6000 GPU (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`). |
| `--maintenance-policy` | Determines what happens during host maintenance. |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Automatically restarts the instance if it crashes. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: runs a custom script at boot. |
| `--tags` | Network tags for firewall rules (e.g., allow HTTP/HTTPS). |
| `--scopes` | IAM scopes for the instance’s service account. |
| `--service-account` | Optional: use a specific service account. |
| `--quiet` | Suppress interactive prompts. |

> **Tip:** If you prefer the REST API instead of `gcloud`, you can POST to `https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances` with a JSON body that mirrors the flags above. The `accelerators` field would look like:
> ```json
> "accelerators": [
>   {
>     "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
>     "acceleratorCount": 1
>   }
> ]
> ```

Make sure you have the **Compute Engine API** enabled and the **NVIDIA GPU drivers** installed on the instance (you can add a startup script to install them automatically).
